explanation:
[EFFECT] Non-holidays (value = 0) produce a contribution tightly clustered at essentially zero — the model treats a regular day as neutral. On holidays (value = 1), the contribution scatters widely from about −1.2 to +0.5, with the bulk of points below zero (median roughly −0.25 to −0.40), so holidays tend on average to suppress demand relative to regular days, though with considerable variability.
[IMPORTANCE] Because the vast majority of hours are non-holidays and sit at zero contribution, the mean influence of this feature is modest overall; however, its range on actual holiday hours is substantial (~1.3 log-units), placing it in the middle of the importance ranking.
[RECOMMENDATION] Plan your staffing and bike availability primarily around the hour of the day — the evening peak (around 5–6 pm) and the morning shoulder (around 8 am) drive the largest swings in demand — and use temperature as the key weather signal, targeting comfortable mild days (~20–25 °C) for maximum expected ridership and scaling back during cold or very hot spells.
